about: Which of a workload's pods count as trouble at `now`, and by what cause, as both halves read it: `trouble_cause` in src/tauri/src/commands/overview.rs (the Overview's rows) and `troubleCause` with `countsAt` in src/ui/lib/share/pod-status.ts (a workload's list row, page and peek). Each pod is given as the cluster returns it (`pod`) and as the backend ships it (`row`, which the Rust test holds to what `PodRow` serialises); `warned` marks one its kubelet warned about. A pod's `is` names its cause's `says`, or null where it does not count; a case's `is` is what the workload tells: the cause most share, how many share it, of how many it runs.

cases.name: one pod no node takes beside two Ready again since their short exits: the exits are not why it is short
up between the crashes of a loop, Ready or not, counts by its exits; not Ready for seconds does not count
not Ready long after its short exits counts by its probe; unplaced inside its wait does not count
being set up inside its wait counts only where its kubelet warned
restarted with no exit reported counts; a pod its controller replaced is not among its pods
a container the kubelet cannot pull counts by that, whatever exited before
backing off between runs counts by its exits; Ready with exits an hour old does not count
